title: A separated Noetherian scheme of dimension zero is affine
statement: Let $Y$ be a Noetherian separated scheme [def-pc-scheme] [pqf-def-locnoeth] [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] [def-weil-proper-morphism] of topological Krull dimension $\dim Y\le 0$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], including $Y=\varnothing$. Then $Y$ is affine [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. In particular the trivial invertible module $\mathcal O_Y$ [def-sc-invertible-module] is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module].

source.place: Properties Lemma 0AAX (properties-lemma-locally-Noetherian-dimension-0), followed by Lemma 0CKV (properties-lemma-dimension-zero), final assertion: a quasi-compact separated zero-dimensional scheme is affine

proof.text: If $Y=\varnothing$, the conclusion is immediate. Otherwise, [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal] gives that the underlying space is Noetherian. Since $\dim Y\le0$, [lem-sc-zero-dim-noetherian-finite-discrete] gives that $|Y|$ is finite and discrete.
The scheme is quasi-compact and separated by hypothesis, and its underlying space is finite discrete by step 1. Therefore [lem-sc-finite-discrete-separated-affine] applies and $Y$ is affine.

On an affine scheme the trivial invertible module $\mathcal O_Y$ is ample: $Y$ is quasi-compact by hypothesis, which is condition (1); for condition (2) take $n=1$ and the global section $1$ of $\mathcal O_Y=\mathcal O_Y^{\otimes1}$, whose nonvanishing locus is all of $Y$, which is affine by step 2, so every point $x\in Y$ lies in the affine open $Y_1=Y$.
